title: Two changes to the same lines

terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run the setup to build the repository, then work inside repo/ with git.

tasks.title: Keep both new sailings
tasks.description:
Run `node setup.mjs`, then work inside `repo/`.

Merge `weekend-sailings` into `main`. Both branches added a sailing at the same spot in `timetable.txt`.

The check reads `timetable.txt` in the last commit on `main` and expects:

- no conflict marker lines
- both the 08:00 Seal Bay and the 08:30 Puffin Rock sailings
- every sailing listed in time order
- every other line as it was
nextSteps: Run `node setup.mjs`, `cd repo`, then start the merge without an editor.
Open `repo/timetable.txt` and find the block between the conflict markers.
Keep both sailings in time order and delete the marker lines.
Stage the file once it looks right.
hints: A conflict is a question, not a failure. Here both people were right.
The lines between `<<<<<<<` and `=======` are main's version; the lines between `=======` and `>>>>>>>` are Pavel's.
The file should end up with the 08:00 line followed by the 08:30 line, and no `<<<<<<<`, `=======` or `>>>>>>>` lines anywhere.

tasks.title: Keep both changes to the adult fare
tasks.description:
In the same merge, `fares.txt` conflicts on the adult line: Ines raised the price to 7.00 on `main`, and Pavel labelled the line with the age range `(16+)` on `weekend-sailings`.

The check reads `fares.txt` in the last commit on `main` and expects:

- no conflict marker lines
- one adult line that has both Pavel's label and Ines's new price, written the way Pavel formats it
- the child and bike lines unchanged
nextSteps: Run `git diff` while the merge is in progress to see both versions of the adult line.
Write one adult line that keeps what each side wanted.
Remove the markers and stage the file.
hints: Neither side is wrong. One changed the label, the other changed the number.
Take Pavel's line as the shape, then put Ines's price in it.
The result is a single line starting with `adult (16+)`, followed by the price from main.

tasks.title: Finish the merge cleanly
tasks.description:
Complete the merge with a merge commit.

The check expects:

- the last commit on `main` is a merge with two parents, and `main`'s history contains every original commit from both branches (merge, do not rebase)
- `weekend.txt` from `weekend-sailings` is on `main`, unchanged
- no merge is left in progress and `git status` shows nothing to commit and no untracked files
- you are on `main`
nextSteps: Run `git status` and confirm no paths are listed as unmerged.
Create the merge commit without opening an editor.
hints: Staging resolved files does not end the merge. One more command does.
`git commit` accepts a flag that keeps the suggested merge message and skips the editor.
After `git commit --no-edit`, `git log --graph` should show two lines joining at the top, and `git status` should be clean.
